questions.question: 12 men can finish a work in 15 days. After working for 5 days, 4 men leave. How many more days will the remaining men take to finish the work ?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Remaining work duration for **12 men** = 15 − 5 = **10 days**.

Number of **remaining men** = 12 − 4 = **8 men**.

Apply the **M₁D₁ = M₂D₂** logic for the remaining work:

12 × 10 = 8 × Required Days

Required Days = 120 ÷ 8 = **15 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total number of men (M₁) = 12

Total time (D₁) = 15 days

Number of days worked = 5 days

Number of men who left = 4

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Men × Days

Remaining Work = Total Work − Completed Work

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/10cbd4b138df4d80f0712d585a12bb7b1f55d30eeba3747e6af2ab79ad386038.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Work = 12 × 15 = 180 units

⇒ Work completed by **12 men** in **5 days** = 12 × 5 = 60 units

⇒ **Remaining Work** = 180 − 60 = 120 units

⇒ **Remaining Men** = 12 − 4 = 8 men

⇒ Days taken by **8 men** to finish 120 units = 120 ÷ 8

⇒ Days = **15 days**

**∴ The correct answer is 15 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Chain Rule Formula

The relationship between men, days, hours, and work is given by (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) / W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) / W₂.

Inverse Proportion

For a constant amount of work, the number of **men** is **inversely proportional** to the number of **days** taken (M ∝ 1/D).

Total Work as Man-Days

Total work can always be expressed in **man-days** or **man-hours**, which is the product of the number of workers and the time spent.</p

questions.question: Ajay and Vijay start from the same point and walk at 4 km/h and 5 km/h respectively, in the same direction. What will be the distance between them after 2 hours?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference of their individual speeds.

Relative speed = 5 − 4 = 1 km/h.

Distance gap after 2 hours = Relative speed × Time = 1 × 2 = 2 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 
• Start 
• Ajay (4 km/h) → 8 km 
• 
• Vijay (5 km/h) → 10 km 
• 
• Gap = 2 km 

**Given:**

Ajay's speed = 4 km/h

Vijay's speed = 5 km/h

Time duration = 2 hours

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance covered by Ajay in 2 hours = 4 × 2 = 8 km

⇒ Distance covered by Vijay in 2 hours = 5 × 2 = 10 km

⇒ Since they are walking in the same direction, the distance between them is the difference of distances covered.

⇒ Distance between them = 10 − 8 = 2 km

**∴ The correct answer is 2 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two bodies move in the same direction, their relative speed is calculated as the difference between their individual speeds. Relative speed = S₁ − S₂.

Relative Speed in Opposite Direction

When two bodies move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds. Relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

Distance Formula

Distance is defined as the product of speed and time. The formula used is D = S × T, maintaining corresponding units like km/h and hours.

questions.question: A trader sold an item at a profit of 20%. If the cost price was Rs. 500, find the selling price.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Consider **Cost Price (CP)** as 100%.

Since the **trader** sold the **item** at a **profit** of 20%, the **Selling Price (SP)** is 120% of **CP**.

**SP** = 120% of 500 = 1.2 × 500 = 600.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 600.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Cost Price (CP)** of the item = Rs. 500

**Profit Percentage** = 20%

**Formula Used:**

**Selling Price (SP)** = **CP** × (100 + **Profit%**) / 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5c0b60826899980201bd21b3a11a862b719530c5e344c6cd5ca02f31a58124b2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Profit Amount** = 20% of 500

⇒ **Profit Amount** = (20 / 100) × 500

⇒ **Profit Amount** = 0.2 × 500 = Rs. 100

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = **Cost Price (CP)** + **Profit Amount**

⇒ **SP** = 500 + 100

⇒ **SP** = 600

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 600.**

**__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

**Profit** occurs when **SP** > **CP**. Formula: **Profit** = **SP** − **CP**. **Loss** occurs when **CP** > **SP**. Formula: **Loss** = **CP** − **SP**.

Selling Price for Loss

If an **item** is sold at a **loss percentage**, then **SP** = **CP** × (100 − **Loss%**) / 100.

Calculating CP from SP

To find the **Cost Price** when **SP** and **Profit%** are known: **CP** = (**SP** × 100) / (100 + **Profit%**).</p

questions.question: A regular octagon is paved inside a circular traffic junction. What is the sum of all internal angles?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any **regular polygon** with **n sides**, the sum of all internal angles is calculated using the property (n − 2) × 180°.

An **octagon** has n = 8 sides.

Sum = (8 − 2) × 180°

Sum = 6 × 180° = 1080°.

**∴ The correct answer is 1080°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The polygon is a **regular octagon** paved inside a circular traffic junction.

⇒ Number of sides (n) = 8

**Formula Used:**

Sum of all internal angles of a polygon = (n − 2) × 180°

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6e30de74df0377bb00311bd0252003a3053cc75d04beccaf56237679e1472a2d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total interior angles = (8 − 2) × 180°

⇒ Total interior angles = 6 × 180°

⇒ Total interior angles = 1080°

**∴ The correct answer is 1080°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Interior Angle of a Regular Polygon

Each interior angle of a regular polygon is given by [(n − 2) × 180°] ÷ n. For an octagon, this is 1080° ÷ 8 = 135°.

Sum of Exterior Angles

The sum of the exterior angles of any convex polygon is always 360°, regardless of the number of sides.

Relation between Interior and Exterior Angles

At each vertex of a polygon, the sum of the interior angle and the corresponding exterior angle is always 180°.</p

questions.question: What is the equation of the line with slope -2 passing through the point (1, -3)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the **slope** m = −2 and the **point** (1, −3).

Use the **Slope-Intercept form**: y = mx + c.

Substitute the coordinates: −3 = (−2 × 1) + c.

⇒ −3 = −2 + c ⇒ c = −1.

The required equation is y = −2x − 1.

**∴ The correct answer is y = − 2x − 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Slope** (m) = −2

**Point** (x₁, y₁) = (1, −3)

**Formula Used:**

The **Point-Slope form** of a linear equation is: (y − y₁) = m(x − x₁)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/96d4cd28db0fa6a4629b9ffb60bba003228935fcdad860eef468643e172eedc9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ y − (−3) = −2(x − 1)

⇒ y + 3 = −2(x) − (−2 × 1)

⇒ y + 3 = −2x + 2

⇒ y = −2x + 2 − 3

⇒ y = −2x − 1

**∴ The correct answer is y = − 2x − 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Slope-Intercept Form

Defined as y = mx + c, where m represents the **slope** and c represents the **y-intercept** (the value of y when x = 0).

Slope Formula

If two points (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂) are known, the **slope** m is calculated as (y₂ − y₁) ÷ (x₂ − x₁).

Parallel and Perpendicular Lines

**Parallel lines** have equal slopes (m₁ = m₂). **Perpendicular lines** have slopes whose product is −1 (m₁ × m₂ = −1).</p

questions.question: A large ship consumes 0.2 liters of fuel per km, and a smaller ship consumes 0.15 liters per km. If the large ship travels 500 km and the small ship travels 400 km, what is the total fuel cost at a rate of ₹110 per liter?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total fuel = (0.2 × 500) + (0.15 × 400)

Total fuel = 100 + 60 = 160 liters

Total cost = 160 × 110 = ₹17,600

**∴ The correct option is (2).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Large ship rate = 0.2 L/km, Distance = 500 km

Small ship rate = 0.15 L/km, Distance = 400 km

Fuel price = ₹110 per liter

**Formula Used:**

Total Fuel = (Consumption rate₁ × Distance₁) + (Consumption rate₂ × Distance₂)

Total Cost = Total Fuel × Price per liter

 Large Ship 500 km × 0.2 L/km = 100 Liters Small Ship 400 km × 0.15 L/km = 60 Liters 
• Total Fuel = 100 + 60 = 160 L Total Cost = 160 × ₹110 = ₹17,600 

⇒ Fuel consumed by large ship = 0.2 × 500 = 100 liters

⇒ Fuel consumed by small ship = 0.15 × 400 = 60 liters

⇒ Total fuel consumed by both ships = 100 + 60 = 160 liters

⇒ Cost of fuel per liter = ₹110

⇒ Total fuel cost = 160 × 110

⇒ Total fuel cost = ₹17,600

**∴ The correct option is (2).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unitary Method for Consumption

Total consumption is calculated by multiplying the rate of consumption per unit distance by the total distance traveled (Fuel = Rate × Distance).

Total Cost Calculation

Total Cost = Total Quantity × Price per Unit. In this case, Quantity is the total fuel in liters and Price is the cost per liter.

Fuel Efficiency

Efficiency can also be expressed as distance per liter (km/L), which is the reciprocal of liters per km (L/km). Higher L/km means lower efficiency.

questions.question: What type of number is the sum of sqrt{2} and (3 - sqrt{2})?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum = √2 + (3 − √2)

The irrational terms √2 and −√2 cancel each other out directly.

The remaining value is 3, which is an integer.

Since all integers are rational numbers, the sum is a rational number.

**∴ The correct answer is a rational number.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First number = √2

Second number = 3 − √2

**Formula Used:**

Sum of terms = a + (b − a) = b

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum = √2 + (3 − √2)

⇒ Sum = √2 + 3 − √2

⇒ Sum = (√2 − √2) + 3

⇒ Sum = 0 + 3

⇒ Sum = 3

⇒ 3 can be written as 3/1, which is in the form p/q (where p, q are integers and q ≠ 0).

**∴ The correct answer is a rational number.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Rational Numbers

A number is rational if it can be written as a fraction p/q where p and q are integers and q ≠ 0. This includes all integers and terminating or repeating decimals.

Irrational Numbers

Numbers that cannot be written as simple fractions. Their decimal expansions are non-terminating and non-repeating (e.g., √2, √3, π).

Sum of Irrationals Property

The sum of two irrational numbers is not always irrational. It can be rational if the irrational parts cancel out, as seen in this problem.

questions.question: Two numbers are respectively 20% less and 30% more than a third number. What is the ratio of the two numbers?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Assume the **third number** is 100.

The **first number** (20% less than 100) = 80.

The **second number** (30% more than 100) = 130.

The **required ratio** = 80 : 130 = 8 : 13.

**∴ The correct answer is 8:13.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Let the **third number** be x.

**First number** = x − (20/100) × x

**Second number** = x + (30/100) × x

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/218fd268437ccd0e2758ca4b12e9af24c7b4e24fe4bb4bbe422507ab80ced23f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **First number** = 0.8x

⇒ **Second number** = 1.3x

⇒ **Ratio** = First number : Second number

⇒ **Ratio** = 0.8x : 1.3x

⇒ **Ratio** = 8 : 13

**∴ The correct answer is 8:13.**

**__Additional Information__**

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To simplify calculations, convert percentages to fractions: 20% = 1/5 and 30% = 3/10. If the third number is 1, the first is 1 − 1/5 = 4/5 and the second is 1 + 3/10 = 13/10.

Base Value Selection

In problems where two values are compared to a common **third value**, always assume the third value to be 100 or a multiple of the denominators to avoid decimal calculations.

Ratio Properties

The **ratio** a : b is the same as ka : kb for any non-zero constant k. Multiplying 0.8 : 1.3 by 10 removes the decimal to give 8 : 13.</p

questions.question: A stationery supplier ordered 8 boxes of premium pens and some boxes of standard pens. The price of premium pens per box was twice that of standard pens. When the order was delivered, the number of boxes of premium and standard pens had been accidentally interchanged. This increased the total bill by 25%. What was the ratio of the original number of boxes of premium pens to the original number of boxes of standard pens?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the price of standard and premium pens be 1 and 2 units respectively, and standard boxes ordered be y.

Original Cost = (8 × 2) + (y × 1) = 16 + y

New Cost (after interchange) = (y × 2) + (8 × 1) = 2y + 8

Given a 25% increase in the bill, the multiplier is 5/4, giving: (2y + 8) / (16 + y) = 5 / 4

⇒ 8y + 32 = 5y + 80 ⇒ 3y = 48 ⇒ y = 16

Ratio of Premium to Standard = 8 : 16 = 1 : 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Original number of premium boxes = 8

Price of a premium box is twice the price of a standard box.

New total bill is 25% more than the original bill due to interchanged quantities.

questions.question:
Consider the following two statements, labeled Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Evaluate them and choose the appropriate answer from the given options.**
Assertion (A):** Two non-intersecting and non-touching circles have four common tangents.**
Reason (R):** Two direct and two transverse tangents can be drawn between such circles.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true

questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For two **non-intersecting** and **non-touching** circles, the distance between their centers (d) is always greater than the sum of their radii (r₁ + r₂).

In this relative position, exactly **4 common tangents** exist: 2 **Direct Common Tangents** (which do not cross the line joining centers) and 2 **Transverse Common Tangents** (which cross the line joining centers).

Since the reason (R) correctly breaks down the total count (A) into its components, both are true and R is the correct explanation.

**∴ The correct answer is Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Two circles are **non-intersecting** and **non-touching**.

**Formula Used:** Number of common tangents depends on the distance between centers (d) relative to radii r₁ and r₂. For d > r₁ + r₂, the number of tangents is 4.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/23390350abcbac65beb36e88d6efdef76f6b78b8767cbc5aa85f061680c660ca.png] 

⇒ Let the distance between centers be **d** and radii be **r₁** and **r₂**.

⇒ For **non-intersecting** and **non-touching** circles, the circles are placed apart such that d > r₁ + r₂.

⇒ In this case, we can draw two tangents on the outer sides that do not intersect the line segment O₁O₂, known as **Direct Common Tangents (DCT)**.

⇒ We can also draw two tangents that cross each other and intersect the line segment O₁O₂, known as **Transverse Common Tangents (TCT)**.

⇒ Total common tangents = 2 (Direct) + 2 (Transverse) = 4.

⇒ Thus, **Assertion (A)** is correct as there are 4 tangents, and **Reason (R)** is correct as it accurately describes the types of these 4 tangents.

**∴ The correct answer is Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Common Tangents and Circle Positions

If d = r₁ + r₂ (circles touch externally), there are 3 common tangents (2 direct, 1 transverse). If d = |r₁ − r₂| (touch internally), there is only 1 common tangent.

Length of Direct Common Tangent (DCT)

The length is calculated using the formula: Length = √[d² − (r₁ − r₂)²].

Length of Transverse Common Tangent (TCT)

The length is calculated using the formula: Length = √[d² − (r₁ + r₂)²]. Note that TCT only exists if d ≥ r₁ + r₂.</p

questions.question: A sum invested at rate r% simple interest for 5 years yields ₹1,500 as interest. If the rate were increased by 2% p.a. (i.e. r + 2% p.a.) for the same period, the interest would be ₹ 1,800. What was the original principal?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Increase in **Interest** = ₹1,800 − ₹1,500 = ₹300

Total Increase in **Rate** over **5 years** = 2% × 5 = 10%

This 10% of **Principal** is equal to the increase in **Interest**.

10% of **Principal** = ₹300 ⇒ 100% (**Principal**) = ₹3,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3000.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Time (T)** = 5 years

**Initial Interest (I₁)** = ₹1,500 at **Rate (r%)**

**New Interest (I₂)** = ₹1,800 at **Rate (r + 2)%**

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/758e2eb3ef1b15ebff5505b58e499ce2590e558bdabd08d64575d5a853c02713.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **Principal** be P.

⇒ Case 1: 1500 = (P × r × 5) ÷ 100 --- (i)

⇒ Case 2: 1800 = (P × (r + 2) × 5) ÷ 100 --- (ii)

⇒ Subtracting (i) from (ii):

⇒ 1800 − 1500 = [(P × (r + 2) × 5) ÷ 100] − [(P × r × 5) ÷ 100]

⇒ 300 = (P × 5 ÷ 100) × (r + 2 − r)

⇒ 300 = (5P ÷ 100) × 2

⇒ 300 = 10P ÷ 100

⇒ 300 = P ÷ 10

⇒ P = 300 × 10 = ₹3,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹3000.**

**__Additional Information__**

Direct Proportionality in Simple Interest

Simple Interest is directly proportional to the **Principal**, **Rate**, and **Time**. If any one factor changes while others are constant, the interest changes by the same ratio.

Change in Interest Formula

ΔSI = (P × ΔR × T) ÷ 100. This formula helps find the **Principal** when the difference in interest due to a rate change is known.

Relationship of Amount and Interest

**Amount** = **Principal** + **Simple Interest**. An increase in **Rate** increases the **Interest**, which in turn increases the final **Amount**.

questions.question: A cylinder having radius of 5 cm and a height of 10 cm. Find its volume. (π = 3.14)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Volume** of **cylinder** = π × r² × h

Given: **radius** (r) = 5 cm, **height** (h) = 10 cm, **π** = 3.14

**Volume** = 3.14 × 5² × 10

**Volume** = 3.14 × 25 × 10 = 785 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 785 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Radius** (r) = 5 cm

**Height** (h) = 10 cm

**π** = 3.14

**Formula Used:**

**Volume** of **Cylinder** = πr²h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4d71b46bc02a9dd69f4454e778035dbe7d4217400aaae1ffcda2c6345ebf748f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Volume** = 3.14 × (5)² × 10

⇒ **Volume** = 3.14 × 25 × 10

⇒ **Volume** = 78.5 × 10

⇒ **Volume** = 785 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 785 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area (CSA) of Cylinder

The area of the side surface of the **cylinder** is given by 2πrh.

Total Surface Area (TSA) of Cylinder

The sum of the **CSA** and the areas of the two circular bases: 2πr(h + r).

Volume of a Cone

A cone with the same **radius** and **height** as a **cylinder** has exactly one-third of its **volume**: (1/3)πr²h.

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is a perfect square and a multiple of 4?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **square** of an **even number** is always a **multiple of 4**, while the square of an odd number is always odd.

Identify the even number among the perfect squares: 625 (odd), 256 (even), 225 (odd), 169 (odd).

Only **256** is an even perfect square (16²).

Checking divisibility: 256 ÷ 4 = 64 (Remainder = 0).

**∴ The correct answer is 256.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given numbers:** 625, 256, 225, 169

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/527ba7fa4df13730b0b634928cd309b07d1efb2ad8f301202ed492a466c34822.png] 

**Step 1:** Determine if each option is a **perfect square**.

⇒ √625 = 25 (Integer)

⇒ √256 = 16 (Integer)

⇒ √225 = 15 (Integer)

⇒ √169 = 13 (Integer)

All given options are perfect squares.

**Step 2:** Check which square is a **multiple of 4**.

⇒ 625 ÷ 4 = 156.25 (Not a multiple)

⇒ 256 ÷ 4 = 64 (Multiple of 4)

⇒ 225 ÷ 4 = 56.25 (Not a multiple)

⇒ 169 ÷ 4 = 42.25 (Not a multiple)

**∴ The correct answer is 256.**

**__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 4

A number is divisible by 4 if its last two digits are divisible by 4 or if the last two digits are 00. In 256, 56 is divisible by 4 (14 × 4 = 56).

Property of Even Squares

The square of an even number (2n)² = 4n² is always divisible by 4. Conversely, the square of an odd number (2n+1)² always leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by 4.

Ending Digits of Squares

Perfect squares can only end with the digits 0, 1, 4, 5, 6, or 9 in the unit place. A number ending in 2, 3, 7, or 8 cannot be a perfect square.</p

DR of 35³ = 8³ = 512 ⇒ 8

DR of 53³ = 8³ = 512 ⇒ 8, and DR of 159 = 1 + 5 + 9 = 15 ⇒ 6

Expression DR = 8 + 8 − 8 + 6 = 14 ⇒ 5

Checking options, DR of −20659 is 9 − (2 + 0 + 6 + 5 + 9) = 9 − 22 ⇒ 9 − 4 = 5. (Matches perfectly)

**∴ The correct answer is -20659.**

44³ + 35³ − 53³ + 159

Summing the positive numbers:

⇒ 128218 − 148877

Subtracting the larger value from the smaller value:

⇒ −20659

questions.question: A man on a lighthouse that stands 50 meters tall is observing a boat moving away from it. Over the course of 10 seconds, the angle of depression to the boat shifts from 60^circ to 30^circ . What is the approximate speed of the boat?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Distance covered by boat = Height × (cot θₛₘₐₗₗₑᵣ − cot θₗₐᵣgₑᵣ)

Distance = 50 × (cot 30° − cot 60°) = 50 × (√3 − 1/√3) = 50 × (2/√3) = 100/√3 m

Distance ≈ 100 / 1.732 = 57.736 m

Speed = Distance ÷ Time = 57.736 ÷ 10 = 5.7736 m/s ≈ 5.8 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 5.8 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Height of lighthouse (AB) = 50 m, Time (t) = 10 s, Initial angle (θ₁) = 60°, Final angle (θ₂) = 30°.

**Formula Used:** tan θ = Perpendicular ÷ Base; Speed = Distance ÷ Time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a40b78053586cc6f22957311dc3bb39b3d57ef46acc38c465a53456c133c555.png] 

⇒ In triangle ABC, tan 60° = AB ÷ BC

⇒ √3 = 50 ÷ BC ⇒ BC = 50 ÷ √3 m

⇒ In triangle ABD, tan 30° = AB ÷ BD

⇒ 1/√3 = 50 ÷ BD ⇒ BD = 50√3 m

⇒ Distance (CD) = BD − BC = 50√3 − 50/√3 = (150 − 50) ÷ √3 = 100 ÷ √3 m

⇒ Speed = (100 ÷ √3) ÷ 10 = 10 ÷ √3 m/s

⇒ Speed ≈ 10 ÷ 1.732 = 5.7736 m/s ≈ 5.8 m/s

**∴ The correct answer is 5.8 m/s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angle of Depression

The angle formed between the horizontal line and the line of sight when looking down at an object. It is numerically equal to the angle of elevation from the object to the observer.

Trigonometric Ratios

Standard values used: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 60° = √3, cot 30° = √3, and cot 60° = 1/√3.

Speed-Distance Relation

Speed is defined as the distance traveled per unit of time (Speed = Distance ÷ Time). Ensure units are consistent (meters and seconds result in m/s).

Apply BODMAS rule: Bracket → Multiplication → Addition → Subtraction.

62 + 71 − 49 + (34 × 2) − (33 + 14)

⇒ 62 + 71 − 49 + 68 − 47

⇒ (62 + 71 + 68) − (49 + 47) = 201 − 96 = 105

**∴ The correct answer is 105.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given expression: 62 + 71 − 49 + 34 × 2 − (33 + 14)

Method: Follow BODMAS sequence (Brackets, Of, Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction).

⇒ 62 + 71 − 49 + 34 × 2 − 47

⇒ 62 + 71 − 49 + 68 − 47

⇒ 133 − 49 + 68 − 47

⇒ 84 + 68 − 47

⇒ 152 − 47

⇒ 105

**∴ The correct answer is 105.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

BODMAS Rule

It specifies the order of operations: Brackets first, then Of (powers/roots), Division and Multiplication (left to right), and finally Addition and Subtraction (left to right).

Grouping Technique

In long addition/subtraction, group all positive numbers and all negative numbers separately before the final subtraction to minimize calculation errors.

Brackets Priority

The order of solving brackets is: Vinculum (Bar), Round brackets (), Curly brackets {}, and then Square brackets [].

questions.question: If a man purchases an article marked at Rs. 1200 with two successive discounts of 10% and 5%, what is the final price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Ratio Method** for successive discounts:

10% discount = 1/10 ⇒ Ratio is 10 : 9

5% discount = 1/20 ⇒ Ratio is 20 : 19

Overall Ratio = (10 × 20) : (9 × 19) = 200 : 171

200 units = ₹1200 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹6

171 units = 171 × 6 = ₹1026

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1026.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Marked Price (MP)** = ₹1200

**First Discount (D₁)** = 10%

**Second Discount (D₂)** = 5%

**Formula Used:**

Final Price = MP × (100 − D₁)/100 × (100 − D₂)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3ff5d95e9ed0b1f07197fc48e2617396864b880ad22c1a5587f0fc91b2834362.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Price after 10% discount = 1200 − (10% of 1200)

⇒ Price after 10% discount = 1200 − 120 = ₹1080

⇒ Price after 5% discount = 1080 − (5% of 1080)

⇒ Price after 5% discount = 1080 − 54

⇒ Final Price = ₹1026

∴ The final purchase price of the article is ₹1026, which matches **Option (2)**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1026.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Single Equivalent Discount

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the single effective discount is calculated as [a + b − (a × b / 100)]%.

Marked Price (MP) and Selling Price (SP)

Selling Price is the final amount paid after deducting all discounts from the Marked Price: SP = MP − Discount.

Discount Percentage

Discount % = (Total Discount / Marked Price) × 100.

questions.question: The average of the squares of the first 10 natural numbers is A. If each number is doubled first, and then squared, what is the new average?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **average** of the **squares** of the first 10 natural numbers is given by A = [(n + 1)(2n + 1)] ÷ 6.

For n = 10, A = (11 × 21) ÷ 6 = 38.5.

If each number is **multiplied** by a factor k, its square is multiplied by **k²**.

Here, numbers are **doubled** (k = 2), so each square becomes 2² = 4 times the original square.

New Average = 4 × A = 4 × 38.5 = 154.

**∴ The correct answer is 154.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First 10 **natural numbers** (1, 2, 3, ..., 10), Average of squares = A.

**Formula Used:** Sum of **squares** of first n natural numbers = [n(n + 1)(2n + 1)] ÷ 6.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1c4354b20fa05d3876d78a13cadb4273278cbc2447e6323da1b03aadc5762a67.png] 

⇒ Sum of squares of first 10 numbers = [10 × (10 + 1) × (2 × 10 + 1)] ÷ 6

⇒ Sum = (10 × 11 × 21) ÷ 6 = 385

⇒ Original Average A = 385 ÷ 10 = 38.5

⇒ When each number (x) is **doubled** and **squared**, the term becomes (2x)² = 4x²

⇒ New Sum = 4 × (1² + 2² + ... + 10²) = 4 × 385 = 1540

⇒ New Average = 1540 ÷ 10 = 154

**∴ The correct answer is 154.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of First n Natural Numbers

The sum of first n **natural numbers** is calculated using the formula Sₙ = n(n + 1) ÷ 2.

Sum of Cubes of First n Natural Numbers

The sum of the **cubes** of the first n natural numbers is the square of their sum: [n(n + 1) ÷ 2]².

Effect of Scaling on Average

If every observation in a data set is **multiplied** by a constant k, the **mean** (average) is also multiplied by k.</p

questions.question: What is the simplified value of the expression (785 times 785 times 785 + 215 times 215 times 215)/(785 times 785 - 785 times 215 + 215 times 215) ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The expression is in the form (a³ + b³) / (a² − ab + b²).

This algebraic structure always simplifies to (a + b).

Here, a = 785 and b = 215.

Result = 785 + 215 = 1000.

**∴ The correct answer is 1000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression = (785 × 785 × 785 + 215 × 215 × 215) / (785 × 785 − 785 × 215 + 215 × 215)

**Formula Used:**

a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let **a** = 785 and **b** = 215.

⇒ The numerator is (a × a × a + b × b × b) = a³ + b³.

⇒ The denominator is (a × a − a × b + b × b) = a² − ab + b².

⇒ Expression = (a³ + b³) / (a² − ab + b²)

⇒ Expression = [(a + b)(a² − ab + b²)] / (a² − ab + b²)

⇒ Expression = a + b

⇒ Value = 785 + 215 = 1000

**∴ The correct answer is 1000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Two Cubes

The identity a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) is used to simplify expressions where the sum of cubes is divided by its quadratic factor.

Difference of Two Cubes

The identity a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²) is similar and results in (a − b) when divided by its quadratic component.

Cube of a Sum

(a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b), which is different from the sum of individual cubes.

Difference of Squares

a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b), a fundamental identity for simplifying products and factors.</p

questions.question: A, B, and C invest in a business. A invests Rs 20,000, B invests Rs 25,000, and C invests Rs 30,000. What is the total profit if the share of B is Rs 5,000?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **investment** of **A** : **B** : **C** = 20,000 : 25,000 : 30,000 = 4 : 5 : 6

Total units of **profit** = 4 + 5 + 6 = 15 units

Given, **B**’s **profit share** (5 units) = ₹5,000

1 unit = ₹1,000

Total **profit** = 15 units × ₹1,000 = ₹15,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹15,000.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Investment of **A** = ₹20,000

Investment of **B** = ₹25,000

Investment of **C** = ₹30,000

Share of **B** in **profit** = ₹5,000

**Formula Used:**

In a **partnership**, **Profit Ratio** = Ratio of (Investment × Time)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eb11a80482cf46aacfe011035e0152e3cd6231fb5a77002320417438df70e8bd.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Profit Ratio (A : B : C) = 20,000 : 25,000 : 30,000

⇒ Profit Ratio = 4 : 5 : 6

⇒ Let the **profit shares** be 4x, 5x, and 6x respectively.

⇒ Given, **B**’s share = 5x = 5,000

⇒ x = 5,000 ÷ 5 = 1,000

⇒ Total **profit** = 4x + 5x + 6x = 15x

⇒ Total **profit** = 15 × 1,000 = 15,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹15,000.**

**__Additional Information__**

Ratio of Profits

In any partnership, the ratio of **profit** distribution is calculated as: P₁ : P₂ = (I₁ × T₁) : (I₂ × T₂), where I is **investment** and T is **time**.

Simple Partnership

When the **time period** for all investments is the same, the **profit** is shared simply in the ratio of the **capitals** invested.

Compound Partnership

When **partners** invest their capital for different **time periods**, the profit is shared in the ratio of the product of capital and time.

questions.question: A right circular cone has a base circumference of 44 cm and a slant height of 14 cm . Find its curved surface area.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **Curved Surface Area (CSA)** of a cone can be directly calculated using the **base circumference** (C) and **slant height** (l).

Formula: **CSA** = (1/2) × **Circumference** × **Slant Height**

⇒ CSA = (1/2) × 44 × 14

⇒ CSA = 22 × 14 = 308 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 308 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Base **circumference** of the cone = 44 cm

**Slant height** (l) of the cone = 14 cm

**Formula Used:**

1. Circumference = 2 × π × r

2. **Curved Surface Area (CSA)** = π × r × l

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7858a92f4132b443f71ef95ad05be60c4a59da6170136d23a1de1767fe03b816.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 2 × (22/7) × r = 44

⇒ (44/7) × r = 44

⇒ r = (44 × 7) / 44

⇒ r = 7 cm

Now, calculating the **Curved Surface Area**:

⇒ CSA = π × r × l

⇒ CSA = (22/7) × 7 × 14

⇒ CSA = 22 × 14

⇒ CSA = 308 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 308 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of a Cone

It is the sum of the curved surface area and the base area: TSA = πr(l + r).

Volume of a Cone

The space occupied by the cone is given by the formula: V = (1/3)πr²h, where h is the vertical height.

Slant Height Relation

The relationship between slant height (l), radius (r), and height (h) is: l² = r² + h² or l = √(r² + h²).</p

questions.question: The parallel sides of a trapezium differ by 4 cm. Its height is 8 cm and the area is 192 cm². What are the lengths of the parallel sides?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Sum of parallel sides** = (2 × **Area**) ÷ **Height**

Sum = (2 × 192) ÷ 8 = 48 cm

Larger side = (Sum + Difference) ÷ 2 = (48 + 4) ÷ 2 = 26 cm

Smaller side = (Sum − Difference) ÷ 2 = (48 − 4) ÷ 2 = 22 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 22 cm and 26 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Area** of trapezium = 192 cm²

**Height** (h) = 8 cm

Difference between **parallel sides** = 4 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area of Trapezium = (1/2) × (Sum of parallel sides) × Height

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cf19a4c43d5ba223f728ac5189346df7dae9efbe423cfd6e5dee30aac9ce8a7a.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the **parallel sides** be 'a' cm and 'b' cm.

⇒ b − a = 4

⇒ Area = (1/2) × (a + b) × 8

⇒ 192 = 4 × (a + b)

⇒ a + b = 192 ÷ 4

⇒ a + b = 48

Adding the two equations (b − a = 4 and a + b = 48):

⇒ 2b = 52

⇒ b = 26 cm

Substituting b = 26 in a + b = 48:

⇒ a + 26 = 48

⇒ a = 22 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 22 cm and 26 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Trapezium

A trapezium is a **quadrilateral** with at least one pair of **parallel sides**. The sum of the **interior angles** is 360°.

Median of a Trapezium

The **median** (midsegment) connects the midpoints of the non-parallel sides and its length is the **average** of the parallel sides: Median = (a + b) ÷ 2.

Isosceles Trapezium

If the **non-parallel sides** are equal in length, it is called an **isosceles trapezium**, and its base angles are equal.</p

questions.question: If cos A+sin A=(5)/(4), find tan A.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Given **sin A + cos A = 5/4**.

Squaring both sides: 1 + **sin 2A** = 25/16 ⇒ sin 2A = 9/16.

We know that **sin 2A = 2 tan A / (1 + tan² A)**.

Substituting values: 9/16 = 2t / (1 + t²) ⇒ **9t² − 32t + 9 = 0**.

⇒ 9 tan² A − 32 tan A + 9 = 0

⇒ Using **Quadratic Formula**: tan A = [32 ± √(32² − 4 × 9 × 9)] / (2 × 9)

⇒ tan A = [32 ± √(1024 − 324)] / 18 = [32 ± √700] / 18

⇒ tan A = [32 ± 10√7] / 18 = (16 ± 5√7) / 9

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Pythagorean Identity

For any angle A, the sum of the squares of sine and cosine is always 1: sin² A + cos² A = 1.

Double Angle Formulas in terms of tan A

sin 2A = 2 tan A / (1 + tan² A) and cos 2A = (1 − tan² A) / (1 + tan² A).

Sum and Product of Roots
